what: Illumina makes the machines that read DNA. Laboratories buy its sequencers and then keep buying the reagent kits that run on them, which is where most of the profit comes from.
customers: Research institutions, pharmaceutical companies, clinical and diagnostic laboratories worldwide.
money: reagent kits and flow cells used on its instruments
moat: An installed base of sequencers that run only its consumables, backed by data pipelines and clinical validations built around its output format.
risks: Revenue has fallen slightly for two years as research budgets tightened
China has restricted purchases of its sequencers
MGI and others are competing on price in a way they could not before
The costly Grail acquisition was unwound after regulators objected
opportunities: Gross margin of 66% with a 19% operating margin after cost reductions
Analysts see about 22% upside from current levels
Clinical sequencing, especially in cancer, grows faster than research use
watch: Consumable revenue per installed instrument and high-throughput sequencer placements.
